discoveries.test: Report digits 5–9 in multiple games, both early and late, across different private digit values. Log mod 7 values and acceptance outcomes.
discoveries.prediction: High-magnitude reports (e.g., 7, 8) will sometimes be accepted and sometimes rejected. Acceptance correlates with audit target alignment, not with being out-of-range.

instructions: Do not assume that because one out-of-range report succeeded, all out-of-range reports will succeed. discoveries.prediction: If a pattern exists, it will emerge after 3–4 games of systematic logging. If no pattern emerges, the target may be random, dependent on private information not revealed, or adversarially chosen.

playbook.strategy: This game exposed flaws in the escalation-heavy strategy of the prior playbook. Four consecutive rejections with no score reinforces that the audit target is not obvious and that blind escalation is not a path to victory. In the next game, prioritize *information gathering* over *score maximization*: (1) Round 1, report your true digit and note the outcome. (2) Round 2, if accepted, stay close to truth; if rejected, try a small deviation (+1 or +2) to probe. (3) Round 3, either request [inspect: ledger] if you sense a pattern (spending the round but potentially learning target logic), or make a larger move if you have gathered enough data. (4) Round 4, commit to your best guess or, if tied/losing, escalate. The playbook's prior 'digit_range_is_permissive' discovery is now marked unreliable: prior success with digit 7 may have been coincidence, not proof. Do not assume out-of-range reports are safe. Track all (round, reports, mod 7 sum, accept/reject) outcomes in a table across games to search for a hidden pattern. Do not amend reports unless you have strong evidence that the amendment will move closer to the target; amendments still cost rounds and still face audit risk.
